title: The global search PR queried MailAccount and MailRule with plain .objects.filter() behind only a model-level has_perm check, unlike the owner-aware get_objects_for_user_owner_aware() it used for tags and correspondents, so users see other users' mail accounts and rules.

findings.explanation: All database access uses Django ORM query methods (filter, get) with parameters supplied as arguments, not string concatenation or raw SQL. No use of .raw() or manual query construction.

evidence.content:
docs = all_docs.filter(title__icontains=query)[:OBJECT_LIMIT]
...
results = s.search(q, limit=OBJECT_LIMIT)

docs = docs | all_docs.filter(id__in=[r["id"] for r in results])

findings.explanation: The GlobalSearchView checks that the user is authenticated and verifies per‑object permissions before querying each model (e.g., has_perm('documents.view_document'), get_objects_for_user_owner_aware, owner filter). No object is fetched solely by a user‑controlled ID without an ownership or permission check.
